query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small addition (e.g. 2–5 wt.%) of aluminum into equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr during casting will form a continuous, adherent alumina scale at high temperatures which significantly slows oxygen ingress and oxidation, while preserving the alloy’s room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy with established ductility (8–16% at room temperature) and high-temperature yield strength (163–530 MPa at 1000 °C) but inadequate oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Addition of 2–5 wt.% aluminum into the alloy during melting/casting.
generation.conditions: Exposure in air at temperatures up to 800 °C for 5 hours; mechanical testing under similar loading and strain rate conditions (10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹) for both room and high-temperature performance.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, protective Al2O3 (alumina) scale on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Aluminum in the alloy preferentially oxidizes to form a stable, slow-growing alumina scale that acts as a diffusion barrier against oxygen, thus mitigating further oxidation of the underlying refractory elements without compromising the alloy’s overall mechanical integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated material, the Al-modified alloy will exhibit significantly improved oxygen resistance (i.e. less oxidation damage) while retaining similar tensile ductility at room temperature and yield strength at high temperature.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits rapid oxidation and loss of protective mechanical properties under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: Intervention effectiveness is expected for exposures up to 800 °C in air for durations around 5 hours. Excess aluminum (beyond ~5 wt.%) might lead to embrittlement or degradation of mechanical performance, and thus the intervention is constrained within this limited addition range.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal aluminum concentration and its precise impact on microstructural stability and oxidation kinetics remain uncertain without experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of cast samples: one set of baseline equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr and one set with 2–5 wt.% aluminum addition. Expose both sets to air at 800 °C for 5 hours under controlled conditions. After exposure, evaluate the surface oxidation via microscopy and measure room- and high-temperature mechanical properties (tensile ductility and yield strength).
measurements: Oxide scale thickness and continuity using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aluminum-added samples do not show a significant reduction in oxide scale growth (i.e. similar or worse oxidation profile) or if they exhibit a marked degradation in room- or high-temperature mechanical properties relative to the untreated samples, the hypothesis will be falsified.
